description: ABOUT YOU We are looking for a Tech Lead for the Frontend Platform Team provides technical leadership for Xsolla’s core platform responsible for powering all user-facing experiences. This role combines deep engineering expertise with people leadership, guiding a team of approximately eight developers. The Tech Lead shapes the platform’s architecture, improves developer workflows, and ensures high-quality, scalable solutions that support storefronts, widgets, and other monetization-focused experiences used across the Xsolla ecosystem. This position requires strong frontend and platform-level experience, the ability to lead complex technical initiatives, and the capability to support predictable, reliable delivery. ABOUT US Xsolla is a global commerce company with robust tools and services to help developers solve the inherent challenges of the video game industry. From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help them fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Grounded in the belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in the mission to bring opportunities together, and continually make new resources available to creators. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. With more paths to profits and ways to win, developers have all the things needed to enjoy the game. For more information, visit xsolla.com. Responsibilities: Provide technical leadership for the Xsolla frontend platform, defining architecture, coding standards, and long-term technical direction. Coach, mentor, and manage a team of ~8 developers, supporting professional growth and maintaining a strong engineering culture. Partner closely with the other Tech Leads working on the same platform to ensure architectural alignment, consistent standards, and unified decision-making. Oversee planning and execution of platform features and improvements, ensuring smooth delivery and high-quality outcomes. Drive modernization, refactoring, and performance enhancements to keep the platform scalable, maintainable, and aligned with product goals. Establish and enforce engineering best practices across coding, documentation, testing, and review processes. Collaborate with product managers, designers, backend engineers, and platform teams to deliver cohesive partner-facing experiences. Ensure strong automated test coverage and reliable CI/CD workflows that reduce manual effort and improve delivery predictability. Leverage automation and AI-assisted tooling to accelerate development, improve consistency, and increase developer velocity. Own operational excellence, including incident response, root-cause analysis, and long-term reliability improvements. Advocate for scalability, performance, security, and observability across the platform’s architecture and tooling. Identify technical risks, estimate complexity, and communicate trade-offs to leadership and stakeholders. Foster alignment with other engineering teams on shared services, APIs, rendering pipelines, and platform interfaces. Qualifications & Skills: 8+ years of software development experience with strong expertise in modern frontend engineering at scale. At least 3 years in a similar tech lead role. Deep hands-on knowledge of React including component architecture, SSR patterns, RSC, and complex UI data flows. Proficiency with and MongoDB for server-side functionality. Strong understanding of modern styling systems and theming approaches (vanilla-extract, styled-components, design tokens). Solid TypeScript practices, including strict typing, shared contracts, and schema validation (Zod or equivalent). Experience with Module Federation Good understanding of bundling and compilation, experience with webpack/rollup/vite/esbuild. Experience with automated testing frameworks (Vitest/Jest) and end-to-end testing (Playwright/Cypress). Good understanding of backend integration patterns (REST, GraphQL, RPC-style APIs). Experience with CI/CD workflows (GitLab CI or similar), private registries, and secure artifact handling. Proven ability to lead engineers, own architectural decisions, and manage delivery for complex platform projects. Nice to Have: Experience building platforms or tooling used across multiple frontend teams (design systems, template engines, configuration frameworks). Experience with react-native/mobile experience Knowledge of performance optimization strategies for client-side and server-side rendering. Understanding of accessibility, internationalization, and semantic UI design best practices. Experience developing SDKs, CLI tools, or developer-facing automation. Familiarity with event-driven UI flows, real-time interfaces, or edge-rendering strategies. Background improving developer platforms, observability stacks, or performance monitoring systems. Comfort with UI-as-data approaches and leveraging AI-assisted/no-code tooling to accelerate feature delivery. Benefits:We are passionate about fostering a supportive environment for our team, so we prioritize the physical, mental, and emotional well-being of our employees and their families through a comprehensive Benefits Program. This includes medical, dental, and vision, PTO, and a personalized career roadmap for each employee. By investing in professional development through training and educational opportunities, we ensure that our team thrives both personally and professionally. Together, we’re not just building a business; we’re cultivating a community that values creativity, collaboration, and the transformative power of play. Equal Employment Opportunity Statement: Xsolla is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by law. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with the Fair Chance Act. description: Our story: The widespread adoption of intelligent technologies powered by automation, AI, ML, and knowledge graphs is accelerating. As these technologies become increasingly accessible, our aim is to make their capabilities empowering, trustworthy, and useful to real people in the real world. Adapter was founded in 2022 by Adam Ghetti and Dr. David Bader, with the support of some of the most esteemed Tier 1 Silicon Valley firms and individual entrepreneurs. We are a small but dedicated team, currently working towards solving a significant problem. We recognize the importance of being early movers in this field, and have assembled a well-supported and passionate team to do so. What we are looking for: We are seeking an engineer experienced in designing and implementing robust systems to ingest diverse, complex data types into large-scale knowledge graphs, who will play a key role in shaping and creating the product, which at its core aims to empower individuals through thoughtful collaboration with intelligent technology. You will partner with a brilliant team of engineers and innovators and will be at the cutting edge of some of the most interesting consumer use-cases for intelligent technologies. description: About Outreach Outreach, founded in 2014, is the only complete agentic AI platform for revenue teams. Outreach infuses agentic AI, conversation intelligence, and assistive AI to power hundreds of use cases across revenue motions. From new logo prospecting to expansions, deal acceleration, driving retention, and forecasting, Outreach AI automates workflows and frees sellers to focus on more strategic conversations and actions. Revenue leaders benefit from connected account visibility, performance insights, and higher forecasting accuracy across every GTM team. World leading enterprise organizations use Outreach to power their revenue teams, including Databricks, SAP, Siemens, and Verizon to name a few. About the job: We are looking for an Associate Applied Scientist to join a dynamic and innovative AI platform team. If you are passionate about applying machine learning to knowledge graphs and reasoning systems at scale, this is an opportunity to build core components of Outreach's per-tenant knowledge graph while developing deep expertise under the guidance of senior scientists. Our team is building a per-tenant contextual knowledge graph that captures the full complexity of each customer's sales environment: accounts, deals, contacts, rep behaviors, competitive landscape, and the signals buried in calls, emails, and CRM activity. This graph powers contextual reasoning across the platform, driving next-best-action recommendations, deal risk signals, coaching suggestions, and competitive intelligence. In this pivotal role, you will design the underlying representations, extraction pipelines, and reasoning layers that make this possible, working closely with cross-functional engineering and product teams to deliver innovative, scalable, and reliable AI capabilities with direct impact on revenue outcomes. This role is ideal for someone with strong ML fundamentals who wants to build deepexpertise in knowledge graphs and applied NLP in a fast-moving product environment. Your Daily Adventures Will Include: Key Responsibilities: Knowledge Graph Design & Construction: Design and implement entity resolution and ontology population within established graph schemas. Write and optimize queries for graph traversal and feature extraction. Own data quality for assigned domains. Information Extraction: Build pipelines that extract structured knowledge from unstructured conversational and document data (sales calls, emails, CRM notes), including coreference resolution, relation extraction, and event detection. Run experiments to compare approaches and improve accuracy metrics. Contextual Reasoning & Recommendation: Implement graph traversal logic and feature queries that feed downstream scoring signals. Build and maintain features for deal risk, next-best-action, or coaching recommendation surfaces. Representation Learning: Train and evaluate link prediction and node classification models using established graph embedding methods. Implement evaluation pipelines and track model performance over time. Domain Modeling: Translate sales concepts, such as deal stages, buyer engagement patterns, rep behaviors, and account health, into graph nodes and relationships under the guidance of senior scientists. Contribute to ontology design and documentation. Cross-functional Collaboration: Work with software engineers to deploy models and pipelines into production. Write clean, tested code. Monitor system health and respond to incidents. Participate in code review and design discussions. Our Vision of You: Qualifications: PhD in a relevant field such as Computer Science, NLP, Machine Learning, or a related discipline with a focus on knowledge representation and reasoning, information extraction and relationship extraction, graph neural networks, recommendation systems, or conversation AI and dialogue systems. MS + 2 years of relevant experiecne will also be considered. Solid engineering fundamentals. You can write production-quality code, not just prototype notebooks. You can write clean, tested Python code. Experience with graph databases or query languages (e.g., Neo4j, SPARQL, Cypher). Demonstrated ability to build and evaluate ML models. You've trained models, measured performance using appropriate metrics, and iterated on results. A track record of building things: whether that's research prototypes that went beyond the paper, open-source contributions, or side projects that required real systems thinking. You understand the gap between a research prototype and a reliable production system, such as monitoring, data drift, latency, and operational excellence. Strong Ownership: Take end-to-end responsibility for research and model development initiatives, from problem formulation and data analysis through experimentation, production deployment, and ongoing performance monitoring, driving outcomes with minimal oversight. Good communication skills. You can explain technical concepts to engineers and product managers. Eager to learn. You are excited to develop deep expertise in knowledge graphs and applied NLP under the mentorship of senior scientists. Nice to Have: Hands-on experience applying knowledge graphs or graph-based learning methods to real-world data in a production setting. Strong fundamentals in at least two of: knowledge graph construction, information extraction, graph neural networks, or recommender systems. Experience working with large-scale unstructured text data (conversational transcripts, email, or similar) Experience with probabilistic graphical models, conversational AI, or sales/revenue domain data Published research at top-tier venues Why Join Us? Greenfield Architecture: Shape the design of a core AI system from the ground up, with the latitude to make foundational technical decisions that define the platform. Depth That Matters: This role genuinely requires PhD-level thinking; you will tackle problems in entity resolution, temporal reasoning, and graph learning that demand it. Applied Impact: Work with real production feedback loops and millions of sales interactions, not just benchmarks; see your models change how thousands of teams sell. High Leverage, Low Bureaucracy: Join a small, senior team where your contributions are visible, your ideas ship fast, and you have direct access to leadership. description: Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment. Join our team and make a difference in patient care. About the Role Parachute Health is building the most complete and accurate catalog of home medical equipment and supplies in the industry, and that catalog is at the heart of our entire platform. Over the last few months, a consultant improved our in-house design standards, style guide, review practices, and an early set of universal merchandising attributes. We are now hiring someone in-house to take that work over and grow it for the long term. As our Catalog Strategist & Taxonomist, you will be the expert on our taxonomy, information architecture, and catalog data model. You will serve as the catalog administrator, set and enforce catalog standards, and own catalog functionality enhancements from requirements definition and justification all the way through operational implementation. Reporting to the SVP of Merchandising Operations, you will partner closely with Operations, Product, Design, and Engineering, to make sure the catalog stays accurate, scalable, and easy to work in as we expand into new categories. The groundwork is fairly new, so you will have a solid base to start from and real room to decide where it goes next. You get to grow the skills of an already highly-motivated Merchandising team and make the group even stronger. You will also influence R&D strategy as we build and enhance our catalog software capabilities. You will work closely with the Cat Crew R&D/engineering team, and partner with our clinical division as we launch new categories together. This role is posted as a 90-day contract with the intent to convert to a full-time employee. What You'll Do Own the standards and structure of the global product taxonomy, category hierarchy, and catalog data model, and evolve them as we expand into new categories. Maintain and evolve core catalog assets, including the global catalog style guide, training about existing and new functionality, glossary, and design review guide. Serve as the catalog administrator: govern attributes, values, naming conventions, and data-quality standards across the catalog. Interview category managers and subject-matter experts to learn each category's ideal state, balanced with a curiosity about current state workarounds and platform limitations. Lead design reviews for category managers and analysts and provide effective feedback. Up-level the merchandising team's catalog and taxonomy skills, continuing the trajectory started with the contract taxonomist. Drive the standardized identification of sourcing/provenance attributes, including manufacturer, brand, and product line. Set the long-term strategic direction for catalog data management, quality, and governance, and act as the senior authority the organization consults on catalog and taxonomy decisions. Partner closely with R&D teams to shape near-term catalog software capabilities. Own catalog functionality enhancement requirements end to end, including definition, business justification, and the case for prioritization, then partner with the Catalog Product Manager and Engineering through development and delivery. Collaborate with our clinical division to launch new categories, making sure the catalog and taxonomy support new clinical use cases. Advance AI-assisted catalog tooling and workflows, such as Claude skills for catalog building and quality monitoring, and codify repeatable processes. About You Deep expertise in taxonomy, information architecture, and metadata or attribute modeling, ideally for a large, complex product catalog. Hands-on experience administering catalog or product information management (PIM) systems and defining data-quality standards. A track record of turning ambiguous catalog problems into clear requirements, and of justifying and prioritizing enhancement work against business impact. description: SS&C is a leading provider of mission-critical, AI-powered technology and services empowering financial services and healthcare organizations to work smarter, faster, and securely. Founded in 1986, SS&C is headquartered in Windsor, Connecticut, and has offices worldwide. More than 23,000 financial services and healthcare organizations, from the world's largest companies to small and mid-market firms, rely on SS&C for expertise, scale, and technology. Job Description Senior Engineer, Ontology Platform About the Team: We are seeking a Senior Engineer to join the Ontology Platform team, reporting to the Ontology Platform Lead, and covering the full engineering lifecycle of the ontology platform: from stewarding the ontology model and building reconciliation/rules logic, through connector and platform engineering, data and warehouse work, and production operations. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants broad ownership across the platform rather than a narrowly scoped specialization: unlike a large infrastructure team where roles split cleanly into specialization tracks, this team is small (5-6 engineers), so each engineer is expected to flex across ontology stewardship, rules engineering, connector/platform work, data engineering, and operations as priorities shift. The ontology platform is built on top of the enterprise's foundational data platform (Airflow, Iceberg, Spark, Flink, Kafka, Nessie, Trino, StarRocks), so you will leverage that infrastructure rather than rebuilding it. Your focus is the layer above it: translating business ontology definitions into concrete structures, building the connectors and mapping/rules logic that bring source systems onto the platform, maintaining the ontology-specific data model and pipelines, and operating the platform in production, including onboarding new sources and supporting business users day to day. Day to Day: Ontology Stewardship & Rules Engineering Partner with business stakeholders to translate their ontology definitions (entities, relationships, attributes) into concrete, implementable structures within the platform, without redefining what the business itself owns. Act as a steward of ontology consistency: identify overlapping or conflicting definitions across business teams and help drive toward a shared, canonical view. Design and build the rules and validation logic that detects breaks (discrepancies between source data and ontology expectations), and continuously improve rule coverage and precision as new sources and use cases are onboarded. Build and maintain reconciliation logic that compares source system data against the canonical ontology and surfaces exceptions in a way business users can triage. Maintain clear documentation of ontology structures, mapping conventions, and rule logic so the model stays understandable as it grows. Connector & Platform Engineering Build and maintain ingestion connectors that bring new source systems onto the ontology platform, working within the frameworks and patterns established by the Engineering Lead. Contribute to core platform services and APIs that support mapping, configuration, and rules management, so business users can define and adjust behavior without engineering intervention per source. Leverage the foundational data platform's ingestion, storage, and compute capabilities rather than duplicating them; escalate capability gaps to the Engineering Lead rather than building bespoke infrastructure workarounds. Adopt and champion an agentic SDLC approach, using AI coding agents and related tooling as a core part of your own development workflow to substantially multiply engineering throughput across connector development, rules/reconciliation logic, and pipeline maintenance, targeting materially higher output than traditional development approaches, not incremental gains. Data & Warehouse Engineering Design and maintain the data models, schemas, and pipelines that store and serve ontology-mapped data for downstream consumption. Build and optimize data transformation logic (ETL/ELT) that moves data from source systems through cleansing, harmonization, and mapping into its canonical ontology form. Ensure data quality, lineage, and performance across the pipeline, from ingestion through to consumption, on top of the foundational platform's storage and compute layers. Operations & Onboarding Own the end-to-end onboarding process for new data sources and business use cases, from initial mapping through to production deployment. Support production operations for the platform: monitoring, incident response, troubleshooting, and resolving data or pipeline issues. Build and maintain runbooks, dashboards, and documentation that make the platform easier to operate and support over time. Work directly with business users during onboarding to help them understand mapping results, breaks, and how to use the platform's configuration tools. Minimum Qualifications: 5-9 years of software/data engineering experience, including exposure to data modeling, data pipelines, and production support for a data platform or similar system. Comfortable working across the full lifecycle of a feature or capability: design conversations with business stakeholders, implementation, deployment, and ongoing operational support, rather than specializing in one slice. Solid data engineering fundamentals: SQL, ETL/ELT patterns, data modeling (relational and/or graph), and experience building or maintaining data pipelines at scale. Experience building integrations or connectors to external/source systems, including handling schema variation and data quality issues at the source. Ability to translate ambiguous business requirements or definitions into concrete technical structures, and to communicate clearly with both business stakeholders and engineers. Experience with production operations: monitoring, incident response, and troubleshooting for data systems. Comfortable working on top of a shared foundational data platform (rather than owning core infrastructure), navigating platform dependencies and escalating capability gaps rather than building around them. Practical, hands-on experience using AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar) as a core part of your development workflow, with a track record of using them to meaningfully increase delivery speed and quality, not just occasional use. Experience in or working with financial services data environments is a plus, given the regulatory and data-quality expectations typical of the domain. Would be Great if You also: Prior exposure to ontology, knowledge graph, or master data management (MDM) concepts. Experience with rules engines or validation/reconciliation frameworks. Familiarity with graph databases or semantic web standards (RDF, OWL, SPARQL). Experience onboarding new data sources or users onto a platform as a repeatable, documented process. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X. We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. Senior Product Designer, Knowledge Graph This is a remote position based in the United Kingdom. The Opportunity: As a Senior Product Designer at Grafana Labs, you will join a growing Product Design organization of more than 25 designers, researchers, engineers, and design leaders distributed across six continents. You will work within a 100% remote R&D organization, so strong, proactive remote communication, collaboration, facilitation, and relationship building skills will be essential to your success. As Senior Product Designer for Grafana Cloud’s Knowledge Graph, you'll design experiences for the context layer of Grafana Cloud that powers our entity graph, entity catalog and RCA workbench. Knowledge Graph automatically discovers services, infrastructure, and databases from the telemetry teams already have, maps how they depend on each other, and runs anomaly detection. description: Learning Commons aims to scale proven teaching and learning practices to benefit every learner by building AI infrastructure that better connects the way students learn to the tools they learn with. The Team At Learning Commons, we operate at the intersection of technology, research, and philanthropy. We pair product development with grantmaking to scale proven teaching and learning practices for the benefit of every learner. We aim to bring learning science into the tools educators and students use every day. Our work is grounded in a deep belief: when technology reflects the realities of classrooms and the science of how students learn, it can meaningfully strengthen teaching and unlock new possibilities for students. The rise of generative AI offers us a once-in-a-generation opportunity to dramatically accelerate the translation of research insights into practical, classroom-ready tools; tools that honor teachers’ expertise, adapt to students’ needs, and make effective learning practices easier to access, implement, and sustain. In today’s fragmented edtech landscape, school districts are often left piecing together products that don’t always align with curricula or instructional needs. While AI holds enormous potential to support teachers and students, it can only deliver on that promise when grounded in research, high-quality educational data, and expert evaluation. That’s why we’re building open, public-purpose infrastructure — datasets, rubrics, and resources — that help raise the standard for educational tools and create more consistent, impactful learning experiences for all students and teachers. The Opportunity We are seeking a Product Manager for a 12-month fixed-term position on the Knowledge Graph team. As a Product Manager on the Knowledge Graph team, you'll help build the data layer for AI in education. AI tools for teachers and students are only as good as the data behind them — and the data they need sits scattered across incompatible formats, academic journals, and proprietary systems, so developers spend their time stitching sources together instead of building. The Knowledge Graph turns that fragmented material into structured, queryable infrastructure — connecting what students are expected to learn, the materials they learn from, and the research on how they learn best, all grounded in learning science. This is a chance to shape a foundation that's still being built. As the graph expands into new subjects and kinds of data, you'll help decide what it covers and how much developers can rely on it, putting you at the center of how research-grounded AI reaches classrooms. It's a rare product surface — few roles combine data modeling, developer experience, and public-purpose education data in one seat — and it rewards a PM who likes to be hands-on and close to the details. You'll have real ownership from the start, with room to grow as the graph scales. What You'll Do Own datasets end to end — Take each dataset from acquisition and licensing through modeling, ingestion, and launch. Write the product docs that define the work clearly enough for engineering to build and ship without rework. Partner with our users — Work closely with the developers and build partners who use the graph to understand their needs and where they get stuck, and spot opportunities for the graph to solve those problems. Help shape the API surfaces they build on, across the REST API and beyond. Plan the work, short and long term — Use partner evidence to shape the roadmap — which data to bring in and how it should grow — and plan the near-term work with engineering so the team ships against a clear, current plan. Work hands-on in the data — Open the source data yourself, run coverage and gap analyses, and verify what ships against the source. Decide how a new source maps onto the graph, when to reuse the model and when to extend it, and set clear, testable acceptance criteria engineers can build against. Keep the cross-functional team aligned — Work across engineering, Trust, partnerships, tech writers, and marketing to move each launch forward and keep everyone working from the same plan. What You'll Bring 3–5 years of product management experience with a track record of shipping, preferably data products, APIs, or developer-facing platforms Education or edtech grounding — You've built products in education or worked in the field, and you understand how curricula, academic standards, and classrooms work well enough to judge what developers serving schools actually need Works well with deep technical experts — You partner with engineers and data experts as a credible peer: you ask sharp questions, pressure-test tradeoffs, and write up complex technical decisions clearly enough for developers to build on Hands-on data fluency and modeling judgment — You personally open raw data files (JSONL, CSV), write queries (SQL, Cypher, or similar), and pull your own counts rather than delegating the check; you can reason about entities and relationships, sketch the nodes and edges for a new dataset, and tell a data gap from a modeling gap Strong product sense — You understand what the people building on your product are trying to do and where they get stuck, and turn that into priorities Compensation The Redwood City, CA base pay range for a new hire in this role is $190,000- $238,000. description: Laboratory Data Ontologist Remote | Canada or US Overview We are seeking a Laboratory Data Ontologist to strengthen the semantic foundation of our platform and the client-specific ontologies deployed on top of it. Labbit is built on a typed entity graph — samples, containers, locations, instruments, pools, and their provenance — and every implementation is, at its core, a modelling exercise: mapping a client's scientific and operational vocabulary onto that graph without losing fidelity. This role sits within our Advisory group. You will spend ~50% of your time billable on client implementation projects as the modelling lead, and the remaining ~50% on internal stewardship — evolving the core ontology, codifying modelling practice, and supporting Sales pursuits. This is not a data engineer role and not a solutions architect role. You are a modeller, steeped in information theory, taxonomy design, and ontology engineering — whose primary deliverables are client and platform ontologies, reference models, and the standards that govern them. Why This Role Matters Our platform's differentiator is a configurable, versioned entity graph with immutable lineage. That model is only as valuable as the discipline behind it: Advisory engagements deepen when modelling is treated as a first-class deliverable rather than a byproduct of configuration. Sales wins when we can quickly show a prospect their world represented cleanly in our model. Implementation delivers faster when client vocabulary maps to reusable patterns instead of bespoke types. Platform evolves coherently when extensions across clients are legible as variants of shared abstractions rather than divergent one-offs. Housing this role in Advisory keeps the practitioner close to real client problems — the billable work is where modelling craft is sharpened — while the non-billable half compounds those learnings into shared assets the whole company draws on. What You Will Do 1. Lead Modelling on Client Engagements (~50% billable) Serve as the modelling lead on Advisory and Implementation engagements where ontology depth is the critical risk Run discovery sessions to elicit and structure client domain models Produce target ontologies — entity types, controlled vocabularies, field taxonomies, workflow decompositions — as billable deliverables Review changeset designs for modelling quality alongside implementation engineers Coach client counterparts on stewardship of their own model post go-live 2. Codify Modelling Practice Across Advisory Author internal standards for taxonomy design, controlled vocabulary governance, and ontology versioning Identify reusable extension patterns across client engagements and promote them into shared libraries Establish review rituals so modelling decisions are traceable and reversible Train Advisory and Implementation staff in applied ontology techniques Build a shared library of domain reference models for our priority verticals (QC manufacturing, clinical genomics, CGT, stability) 4. Support Sales Join late-stage sales cycles to lead ontology discovery sessions with prospects Produce lightweight target models that demonstrate fit without over-committing to configuration Translate prospect terminology (assays, panels, batches, lots) into our model in real time during demos 5. Inform Platform Direction Surface modelling gaps discovered across client work as candidate platform investments Advise Platform Engineering on schema evolution semantics (changeset migrations, deprecations, aliasing) Contribute to decisions about first-class vs. reference-data entities, computed fields, and graph traversal features What You Will Not Do Own application development or feature As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on the GitLab Orbit team, you'll help build and operate a graph data service that supports GitLab Duo agents, analytics, and architecture-level features across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments. You'll join a Rust-first team that values clear ownership, thoughtful system design, and rigorous thinking about data and reliability. The Knowledge Graph service is a Rust backend that builds a property graph from GitLab’s software development lifecycle (SDLC) and code data. It uses ClickHouse, NATS JetStream, and the Data Insights Platform. It exposes secure graph queries and MCP tools used by AI agents and product features. In this role, you’ll deliver features and improvements in well-scoped areas, learn the broader architecture, and contribute to reliability, observability, and operational readiness. In your first year, you’ll take clear ownership of specific components or features (for example, parts of the SDLC indexing pipeline or query paths). You’ll help reduce single points of failure with better tests and runbooks, and you’ll help the team ship analytical services that are easier to maintain and evolve over time. What you’ll do Implement and iterate on backend features in the Rust-based Knowledge Graph service, including changes to the query engine, SDLC and code indexing flows, and API endpoints (including MCP endpoints) under guidance from senior and staff engineers. Maintain integrations between Knowledge Graph and the rest of the GitLab platform, working in areas that touch GitLab Rails, the Data Insights Platform (Siphon, NATS, ClickHouse), and GitLab Duo Agent Platform. Contribute to system design discussions by proposing options, raising questions, and documenting decisions, with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability for analytical graph workloads. Improve the operational maturity of the service by adding or enhancing metrics, logging, runbooks, alerts, and small readiness tasks, and by participating in on-call rotation as appropriate for your level and experience. Collaborate asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security, and AI counterparts to clarify requirements, align on scope, and ship features safely for customers and sustainably for the team. Use AI-assisted development workflows responsibly (for example, using Knowledge Graph-backed agents and internal Duo tooling), and share what works with the team while keeping a strong focus on code quality and correctness. Participate in code reviews, knowledge-sharing sessions, and pairing to both learn from others and help maintain consistent standards across the codebase. Contribute across the stack when needed, including occasional Ruby work for Rails integration and authorization paths, or small frontend changes related to Knowledge Graph features (for example, Software Architecture Map UI plumbing). What you’ll bring Professional experience building and maintaining backend systems in production, with an understanding of reliability, maintainability, and how to support services over time (for example, incident response and follow-ups). Proficiency in at least one modern backend language and strong interest in Rust, with either prior Rust experience or clear evidence you can ramp quickly and deliver in a Rust-first, performance-sensitive codebase. Some exposure to distributed data or analytics systems (for example, OLAP databases, Kafka- or NATS-style messaging, or change data capture (CDC) pipelines), or strong motivation to develop those skills in this role. Interest in graph data modeling and query patterns (property graphs, multi-step (n-hop) traversals, aggregations), and willingness to learn the tools and concepts used in Knowledge Graph over time. Practical experience (or strong interest) using AI tools in day-to-day development, along with a thoughtful approach to validating outputs and integrating AI into your workflow. A language-agnostic mindset and evidence that you can pick up new languages and frameworks as needed (for example, Ruby, Go, or TypeScript/Vue where the work touches adjacent systems). Solid fundamentals in system design for your level, including the ability to reason about trade-offs, ask good questions, and align your implementation work with documented architectural decisions. Comfort working in a low-process, high-ownership environment where you take responsibility for your work, refine problem statements with teammates, and communicate progress clearly in writing across time zones in an all-remote team. We partner with enterprises to reimagine their businesses through intelligent, scalable, and transformative AI—driving measurable outcomes at the very core of their operations. Role: Senior Knowledge Graph Engineer Experience: 5+ years of software/data engineering experience Employment Type: Full-Time (US Remote) Work Location: US Remote (Up to 25% travel to client sites across the US) Role Overview We are looking for a Senior Knowledge Graph Engineer to design, build, and productionize knowledge graph solutions for healthcare and clinical data. Our architecture uses a hybrid graph approach, combining a Labeled Property Graph (LPG) for patient/clinical data with an RDF-based graph for clinical ontology and semantic knowledge. The role will focus on translating ontology and mapping specifications into scalable graph solutions, including data transformation, graph ingestion, concept/entity linking, provenance, validation, and querying. You will work closely with ontology, terminology, FHIR, clinical/domain, and data engineering teams to translate agreed semantic and mapping decisions into robust technical implementations. Key Responsibilities: Develop, implement, build, and maintain production knowledge graph solutions across LPG and RDF graph technologies. Build scalable pipelines to transform healthcare/FHIR data into appropriate graph representations. Implement mappings between patient/clinical data and concepts represented in the clinical ontology. Develop reusable mapping and transformation patterns rather than one-off implementations. Implement consistent approaches for entity identity, canonical identifiers/URI/IRI, relationships, and concept linking. Maintain provenance and traceability between source data, mapping rules, and resulting graph entities and relationships. Develop and optimize graph queries using Cypher and/or SPARQL. Implement automated validation and testing to identify unresolved mappings, inconsistent relationships, and other graph-quality issues. Work with ontology, FHIR, terminology, and clinical SMEs to clarify ambiguous or missing mapping requirements. Participate in technical design, architecture reviews, code reviews, and engineering best practices. Required Qualifications: 5+ years of software/data engineering experience, including hands-on experience with knowledge graphs or graph technologies. Strong understanding of knowledge graph and graph data modeling concepts. Hands-on experience with either: Labeled Property Graphs, such as Neo4j/Cypher or equivalent, or RDF/semantic technologies, such as RDF/RDFS, OWL, and SPARQL. Working knowledge of, or ability to work across, both LPG and RDF graph models. Strong programming skills in Python, Java, or similar languages. Experience building production data ingestion, transformation, or integration pipelines. Experience with graph databases and/or RDF triple stores. Understanding of entity identity, graph relationships, mappings, provenance, and data quality. Ability to translate conceptual models and mapping specifications into production implementations. Ability to work effectively with evolving requirements and cross-functional technical/domain teams. Other Qualifications (OQs) Hands-on experience with both LPG and RDF/semantic knowledge graphs. Healthcare or life sciences data experience. Familiarity with HL7 FHIR, including concepts such as Coding, CodeableConcept, Reference, and Identifier. Experience with ontology-driven data integration or semantic mapping. Experience with SHACL or other graph/semantic validation approaches. Experience with terminology/concept normalization and canonical concept mapping. Familiarity with clinical terminologies such as SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, ICD, or UMLS. Cloud and CI/CD experience. What Sets You Apart? Hands-on experience with both LPG and RDF/semantic knowledge graphs. Healthcare or life sciences data experience with familiarity with HL7 FHIR and clinical terminologies (SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, ICD, or UMLS). Experience with ontology-driven data integration, semantic mapping, and SHACL/semantic validation approaches. Cloud and CI/CD engineering experience in production environment. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X. We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. The Opportunity: As a Senior Product Designer at Grafana Labs, you will join a growing Product Design organization of more than 25 designers, researchers, engineers, and design leaders distributed across six continents. You will work within a 100% remote R&D organization, so strong, proactive remote communication, collaboration, facilitation, and relationship building skills will be essential to your success. As Senior Product Designer for Grafana Cloud’s Knowledge Graph, you'll design experiences for the context layer of Grafana Cloud that powers our entity graph, entity catalog and RCA workbench. Knowledge Graph automatically discovers services, infrastructure, and databases from the telemetry teams already have, maps how they depend on each other, and runs anomaly detection. This gives engineers, SREs, and their agents an up to date picture of their systems. We want anyone to be able to understand a system and resolve an incident faster, without writing queries or maintaining alert rules, not just the one person who happens to know it best. Over time, you will develop deep expertise in your product area and associated customer and user personas, use cases, and workflows, which will enable you to design tailored, role-driven experiences. You will also have an opportunity to contribute to the evolution of the Product Design team at Grafana by coaching and mentoring other designers, collaborating on team internal initiatives, and helping evolve new ways of working, learning, and having fun together as the team scales. functions, as well as other members of the Product Design team Prioritise for delivering impact while balancing business priorities, customer wishes and technical considerations Document user needs description: Standard Job Description The Data and AI Enablement organization is seeking an Enterprise Ontology Product Owner to serve as the connective role between the business functions that own enterprise ontologies and the technical teams that build them. This person ensures that ontology models are grounded in real business meaning, validated by the people who use them, and adopted across AI-enabled experiences, analytics tools, and data products. This is not a technical modeling role. There are dedicated technical teams responsible for building and maintaining ontologies. Instead, this role requires someone who can operate fluently across business functions, translate business language and logic into requirements the technical team can act on, and hold the line on quality, consistency, and adoption. Success depends on deep functional domain expertise, strong facilitation skills, and enough technical fluency to be a credible partner to data engineering and AI/ML teams, not on the ability to build ontologies directly. What You’ll Do Validate and prioritize ontology use cases – ensure models align with business goals, governance policies, and real‑world terminology while coaching business functions to develop competency questions that test scope and correctness. Translate business intent into clear, engineer‑ready requirements and bring stakeholders in as co‑creators through workshops, so data‑engineering and AI/ML teams can build efficiently and without duplication. Collaborate with data product owners and platform teams to guarantee that ontology‑driven data products integrate smoothly with the broader data‑product ecosystem, avoiding conflicts or redundant effort. Drive delivery and quality assurance – track progress, remove blockers, enforce production‑grade data‑pipeline controls, and evaluate the quality and business value of engineered outputs before stakeholder hand‑off. Communicate value and promote adoption – explain modeling decisions in plain language, showcase possibilities with generative‑AI tools, and champion the product to senior leadership and end users. Maintain a continuous feedback loop – gather ongoing stakeholder input, iterate on ontology scope, and update success metrics (adoption, usage, consistency, AI answer quality, business impact) to demonstrate measurable value. Lead cross‑functional delivery teams and partner with business function owners to clarify RACI responsibilities while owning the overall process, coordination, and quality of the ontology. Basic Qualifications Experience working with or on ontologies, knowledge graphs, or semantic data models in a professional capacity. Proven ability to partner with business stakeholders to translate requirements into structured documentation or models. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of explaining technical concepts to non‑technical audiences. What Success Looks Like You’ll know you are successful when business functions trust the ontology as an accurate reflection of how they define their own data and processes, technical teams receive clear, validated requirements to build against, and adoption of ontology‑driven capabilities grows measurably across AI‑enabled experiences, analytics tools, and data products. Success is demonstrated by high usage metrics, concrete business impact, and a continuous cycle of stakeholder‑driven evolution of the product. Must be a U.S. citizen. Basic Qualifications • Experience working with or on ontologies, knowledge graphs, or semantic data models in some professional capacity • Experience partnering with business stakeholders to translate business requirements into structured documentation or models • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to explain technical or structured concepts to non-technical audiences Desired Skills Deep functional domain expertise in one or more enterprise areas (e.g., finance, supply chain, sales, HR, product). Background in product ownership, business analysis, or a coordination‑heavy role focused on validation of use cases. Experience with enterprise data products, platforms, and pipelines (Databricks, data warehouses, MDM, etc.). Experience with data governance, metadata management, or master‑data programs. Familiarity with AI‑enabled experiences, analytics tools, and the broader data‑product ecosystem. Ability to facilitate workshops and engage stakeholders as co‑creators. Understanding of how ontologies improve AI answer quality, semantic search/discovery, and overall business value. Experience with large‑scale enterprise systems (SAP, ERP, etc.) to anchor business terminology in operational data. description: Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit . The Team: The Knowledge Graph Platform team builds the foundational systems that help Reddit understand entities, relationships, and context across its content. We are evolving an advanced, AI-powered knowledge graph into a reliable, scalable platform that enables teams across Reddit to build better experiences on top of shared, high-quality knowledge. This is a high-leverage team at the intersection of data, platform engineering, and AI. Our work supports emerging capabilities such as contextual grounding while creating the contracts, standards, and developer experience that make shared data dependable and easy to use. This team is strategically positioned to impact both ads and consumer roadmaps. Our data is used across ads marketplace models as well as user-facing features on . What You’ll Do: Lead, coach, and develop a team of engineers building Reddit’s Knowledge Graph Platform; create a high-trust, high-performing environment with clear goals and strong technical ownership. Set the technical direction and roadmap for a scalable knowledge graph platform, including data and API contracts, service interfaces, reliability, observability, performance, and developer experience. Establish production-grade operating standards: defining SLOs, implementing quality measures of data within the knowledge graph, governance mechanisms, and safe change-management practices. Partner with engineering, computational linguists, and domain-expert teams to define a shared operating model for ontology, data quality, governance, and platform evolution. Be a steward of data in the KG - ensure the graph has the coverage and freshness needed for priority use cases. Work with our dedicated data labeler team on shared goals around data coverage and quality. Work closely with internal product and engineering teams to understand their needs, prioritize high-value use cases, and increase access to the platform. Drive the next wave of graph-powered capabilities, including opportunities in shopping, search, ads marketplace models, consumer feed models. Stay close to architecture and technical design, helping the team navigate complex system tradeoffs and contribute hands-on when it is the highest-leverage path. Communicate the team’s strategy, priorities, risks, and progress clearly across a distributed, cross-functional organization. Who You Might Be: 8+ years of total software engineering experience, with 2+ years directly managing, coaching, and developing engineering teams. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience). Experience building or operating AI/ML powered, or data-intensive platforms, with a proven track record of leading shared technical systems with multiple internal customers. Strong understanding of how to turn a technical system into a product-like platform: setting an operating model with customers, establishing data or service-level contracts, useful documentation, and a path to self-service adoption. Experience establishing data contracts around quality, lineage, or governance. Strong technical judgment across distributed systems, backend services, data platforms, APIs, reliability, and operational excellence. Comfortable making technical and product tradeoffs in ambiguity, including when a dedicated product manager is not present. Excellent collaborator and communicator who can earn trust with engineers, senior leaders, and partner teams across time zones. Enjoy building clarity and durable operating mechanisms where ownership and processes are still evolving. Excel in evangelization and driving platform adoption cross org. Nice to Have: Master’s or Advanced Degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Computational Linguistics, or a related field. description: About us We are Digital Science and we are advancing the research ecosystem. We are a pioneering technology company, and our vision is of a future where a trusted and collaborative research ecosystem drives progress for all. We believe in better, open, collaborative and inclusive research. In creating the next generation of tools and working in partnership with the community we tackle some of the biggest challenges to research. In order to achieve our vision, we need innovative, inspiring and dynamic people to join our team. Want to join us? Your new role - The Sales Director within the Digital Science Enterprise Segment drives top-line revenue growth by owning the full commercial sales cycle across our integrated portfolio, including Dimensions, Altmetric, ReadCube, Figshare, and metaphacts. This role is responsible for driving pipeline generation, rigorous deal qualification, framing client-centric value propositions, aligning portfolio solutions with enterprise strategic objectives, and leading pricing and contracting negotiations. High priority is placed on a solid conceptual and domain understanding of Knowledge Graph architecture, semantic ontologies, the Semantic Layer, and Agentic AI solutions. The ideal candidate brings a proven sales track record in Life Sciences and excels at bridging high-level enterprise data integration discussions with executive procurement and budget cycles. Technical skills are desired but not required. What you’ll be doing Pipeline Generation & Prospecting Proactively identify, target, and initiate strategic conversations with C-suite leaders, R&D executives, and data architects across Life Sciences, BioPharma, and research-intensive enterprises. Execute territory plans to build a high-volume, high-quality sales pipeline across the full Digital Science capability set. Position Digital Science's unique portfolio advantage—leveraging connections between grants, patents, publications, clinical trials, and knowledge graphs. Deal Qualification & Opportunity Management Apply structured qualification frameworks to evaluate enterprise leads and focus resources on high-probability opportunities. Manage and prioritize enterprise opportunities based on deal value. Map complex decision-making structures to identify executive sponsors, budget holders, and technical evaluators. Seek up-sell and cross-sell opportunities by partnering with Account Managers and Customer Engagement Managers. Coordinated pitches and responses to request for proposals (RFPs). Value Proposition Development & Value Alignment Articulate a compelling, value-based sales narrative focused on the "why" rather than just the "how". Translate complex conceptual capabilities—such as Semantic Web standards, open research workflows, and patent analytics—into clear ROI, de-risked R&D, and accelerated discovery for C-suite leaders. Align Digital Science enterprise solutions with the client’s internal digital transformation, AI readiness, and knowledge management strategies. Pricing & Contracting Negotiations Navigate enterprise procurement, legal, and security review cycles effectively to optimize deal velocity. Lead commercial negotiations, proposal creation, price positioning, and contract execution. Structure multi-product enterprise agreements that maximize deal value, protect margins, and establish long-term customer retention. Portfolio Cross-Selling & Internal Collaboration Act as the commercial lead across products (Dimensions, Altmetric, ReadCube, Figshare, and metaphacts.) Leverage internal resources, including Pre-Sales Specialists (Solutions Architects), Product thought leaders and Marketing resources. Partner closely with colleagues during pre-sales discovery, proof-of-concept (PoC) designs, and technical validations. Work alongside Account Managers to ensure smooth post-sale transitions and identify account expansion opportunities. What you’ll bring to the role Core Commercial Requirements Track Record: 5+ years of demonstrated success in enterprise B2B SaaS sales, solution consulting, or strategic account management with a proven record of hitting quota targets. Negotiation Skills: Proven experience navigating multi-stakeholder procurement and structuring high-value enterprise software contracts. Executive Presence: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to articulate complex technical and data concepts to executive audiences. Domain Expertise (Preferred) Enterprise Information Architecture: Demonstrated commercial or domain familiarity with Enterprise Information Architecture (EIA) frameworks and semantic modeling is highly desired, enabling you to articulate how unifying siloed enterprise data assets into a semantic layer powers context-rich decision intelligence and Agentic AI workflows. Knowledge Graphs & Ontologies: High priority on solid domain understanding of knowledge graphs, semantic ontologies, linked data, and the role of the Semantic Layer in enterprise AI and R&D. Life Sciences Focus: Strong preference for experience selling software, scientific data, or intelligence platforms into Life Sciences, Pharmaceutical, or Biotech accounts. Industry Standards: Familiarity with Resource Description Framework (RDF) concepts and Open Access (OA) publishing models. Technical Background (Desirable) Technical proficiency or hands-on data skills (e.g., SPARQL, Python, graph databases) are a bonus/desired, but not required. The primary focus is commercial execution paired with domain fluency. Travel Willingness and ability to travel 20%–40% for customer meetings, executive briefings, and industry conferences. We're looking for people who are naturally curious about AI and comfortable exploring how it can improve the way we work — you don't need to be an AI expert, but an openness to experiment and adapt is important to us. Don't worry if you don't meet every qualification—let us be the judge! Studies show that many qualified candidates from under-represented groups hesitate to apply unless they meet every single requirement. We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive team and strongly encourage you to submit your application. Living our Values We invest in, nurture and support innovative businesses and technologies that make all parts of the research process more open, efficient and effective. The talent we secure is fundamental to us achieving our vision and our growth plans. The values we live by are: We are brave in the pursuit of better We are collaborative and inclusive We are always open-minded We are from and for the community At Digital Science, our vision is to see research flow seamlessly – trusted, collaborative, and accessible – fueling breakthroughs that push humanity forward. This ambitious mission is one we achieve together, by enabling open, collaborative, inclusive research. We firmly believe that to truly innovate and solve the complex challenges faced by our customers, from researchers and universities to funders and publishers, we need diverse perspectives, experiences, and ideas. A rich mix of voices drives quality insights, fosters enhanced collaboration, and ultimately pushes knowledge forward more effectively. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to building and nurturing a workplace where every individual feels valued and belongs. Beyond recruitment, we strive to cultivate an environment where inclusivity is woven into the fabric of our culture, enabling everyone to be their best self and do their best work. description: About airSlate airSlate is a global SaaS technology company that develops no-code workflow automation, electronic signature, and document management solutions. Our award-winning products - SignNow, pdfFiller, DocHub, altaFlow, Instapage, and US Legal Forms - serve over hundreds of millions of users and more than one million customers worldwide, helping organizations of every size digitize processes, improve efficiency, and transform how they work. We’re in an exciting phase of growth and transformation, with teammates in more than 20 countries across three continents and main hubs in the United States, Poland, Ukraine and Philippines. At airSlate, we’re building value for customers and a culture where growth and innovation go hand in hand. We’re looking for people eager to shape products, scale a company, and thrive in a fast-moving environment. We are looking for a hands-on leader to run Data Enablement. The team that owns how our data is modeled, trusted, and made ready for the business and for AI. You will lead analytics engineers and web analytics specialists, own the semantic layer end-to-end, and turn raw product and event data into curated, well-documented datasets that people can rely on. WHAT YOU WILL DO: Lead and grow the team. Set priorities, coach, and keep a steady delivery rhythm across analytics engineering and web analytics. Own the semantic layer. Design, build and evolve SQL-based models and metric definitions so that one number means one thing across all our products. Raise data curation and automate the routine. Move the team from ad hoc requests to reusable, tested, documented datasets that people and our AI data assistant can query directly, with tracking checks and data-quality monitoring on autopilot. Set standards and partner across the data organization. Modeling conventions, version control, testing and release practices, code review; work with Data Business Partners, Data Science / ML and Data Platform on scope and ownership. Stay close to the code on critical builds. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR: Experience. 5+ years in analytics, data or BI engineering, including 2+ years leading a team or leading others technically. Expert SQL and Python. You set query and performance standards others follow, rewrite expensive queries and explain the trade-offs, handle incremental loads, deduplication and slowly changing dimensions, and own production Python components that other teams depend on. Data modeling and pipelines. You design warehouse and mart models that several teams build on, including a semantic layer, and choose the methodology (star schema, Data Vault or equivalent) to fit the queries it must serve. You optimize and troubleshoot pipelines on a cloud stack such as AWS (Athena, Redshift, Glue) and orchestration tools such as Airflow. Engineering discipline. You set branching and code review standards, require schema and data tests and CI before release, and lead risky changes with a clear rollout and rollback plan. Data quality and data fluency. You design validation that catches problems before stakeholders do, fix root causes rather than symptoms, set documentation standards, and investigate unfamiliar sources before trusting them. Business impact. You design solution options for complex problems, split cross-team work into pieces with a clear definition of done, build dashboards around the decision they support, and become a trusted partner to business leaders. AI in everyday work. You redesign team workflows around AI tools to drive adoption, and evaluate AI outputs for quality, privacy and bias. Leadership and ownership. You own complex team-level projects, make high-impact decisions from complex information, coach people by spotting skill gaps and giving regular feedback, set clear scope expectations, and turn change into actionable steps for the team. Communication. You clarify complex ideas, build consensus across teams and time zones, and communicate in fluent English. Nice to have: experience with dbt or a similar transformation framework (we may adopt one); web analytics and tracking (GTM, GA4); B2B SaaS or document-workflow / e-signature background. What we offer Flexible working environment - Our teams operate across the globe. We value in‑person collaboration in our hubs, but we also embrace remote and hybrid working. You can work from one of our offices in the United States, Poland, Romania or Ukraine, or remotely from many countries. Competitive compensation and stock options - We offer salaries that reflect local market conditions and experience, plus a performance-based bonus system and stock options so you share in the company’s growth. Professional growth and learning - We invest in your development through courses, conferences, and access to learning resources. We encourage career growth and internal mobility, supporting teammates who want to explore new opportunities within airSlate. Health and well‑being - We provide comprehensive benefits tailored to each country, including health coverage, wellness programmes and access to fitness options. We also dedicate quarterly company-wide Mental Health Days, when everyone takes time off to rest and recharge. Family‑friendly culture - Family life is part of who we are, and we embrace it in many forms. From flexibility for parents to our airSlate Junior Club for kids, to company-wide family days and our pet-friendly approach, we’re committed to making work and life easier to balance. Giving back - We support charitable initiatives around the world through the airSlate Care programme. Our current focus includes humanitarian aid in Ukraine and other regions, matching employee donations and supporting causes chosen by our teams. Open communication - We encourage transparent dialogue at all levels. From team discussions to company-wide Q&A sessions with our CEO, we make sure everyone has the chance to be heard and to influence how we grow. description: 1043 - Data Engineer (Neo4j/Cypher/Knowledge Graphs) · Semi-Senior · Remoto · Argentina Ubicación: Argentina Modalidad: 100% remoto Tipo de contratación: Relación de dependencia (full-time) Industria / Proyecto: LegalTech / Inteligencia Legal y Regulatoria con IA Zona horaria: Argentina (ART / UTC-3) Seniority: Semi-Senior (3 a 5 años de experiencia) Conocé Darwoft En Darwoft desarrollamos software que genera impacto real. Somos una compañía tecnológica latinoamericana que trabaja junto a empresas de diferentes partes del mundo, creando soluciones digitales innovadoras, escalables y de alto valor. Nuestra cultura combina excelencia técnica, colaboración, aprendizaje continuo y una fuerte orientación a las personas. La Inteligencia Artificial forma parte de nuestra manera de trabajar, innovar y resolver problemas. Buscamos incorporar nuevas tecnologías para construir mejores productos y potenciar las capacidades de nuestros equipos. Si te apasiona la tecnología, disfrutás resolver desafíos complejos y querés participar en proyectos donde tu trabajo tenga impacto, nos encantaría conocerte. Sobre el rol Estamos buscando un/a Data Engineer Semi-Senior con experiencia práctica en Neo4j, Cypher y modelado de datos en grafos para sumarse a un proyecto innovador de LegalTech enfocado en transformar la manera en que se organiza, conecta y consulta información legal, tributaria, contable y regulatoria. Vas a participar en el desarrollo y evolución de un Knowledge Graph que permitirá relacionar grandes volúmenes de información, identificar conexiones semánticas y potenciar soluciones de búsqueda inteligente basadas en Inteligencia Artificial. Esta posición combina Data Engineering, Graph Databases e Inteligencia Artificial, con un fuerte enfoque en la construcción de soluciones productivas, escalables y mantenibles. Trabajarás junto a equipos de Data Science, Backend e IA para transformar modelos conceptuales, taxonomías y ontologías en estructuras de grafos eficientes que alimenten arquitecturas de recuperación de información como RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation). Buscamos una persona con una base sólida en ingeniería de datos, experiencia real trabajando con Neo4j y motivación por seguir desarrollándose en Knowledge Graphs, búsqueda semántica y GraphRAG. ¿Qué vas a hacer? Modelado de grafos: Diseñar, implementar y mantener modelos de datos en Neo4j, representando entidades, relaciones, jerarquías y estructuras complejas de información. Ingeniería de datos: Construir y optimizar pipelines ETL/ELT para ingesta, transformación, validación y actualización de datos estructurados y no estructurados. Desarrollo con Cypher: Crear y optimizar consultas complejas para recuperación de información, navegación de relaciones y procesamiento de datos en grafos. Implementación de Knowledge Graphs: Transformar taxonomías, ontologías y modelos conceptuales definidos por Data Science en estructuras productivas dentro de Neo4j. Integración con IA y RAG: Participar en la integración de Neo4j con embeddings, búsqueda vectorial y arquitecturas de recuperación semántica. Optimización de performance: Mejorar consultas, estrategias de indexación, consistencia de datos y escalabilidad de la base de grafos. Integración con Backend: Desarrollar integraciones mediante Python o Node.js para conectar los datos del grafo con aplicaciones, APIs y servicios internos. Calidad de datos: Implementar validaciones, controles automatizados y buenas prácticas para garantizar la integridad y confiabilidad de la información. Trabajo interdisciplinario: Colaborar con especialistas en Data Science, Inteligencia Artificial y desarrollo de software para evolucionar la arquitectura de datos. ¿Qué buscamos? Experiencia: Entre 3 y 5 años de experiencia profesional en Data Engineering, Data Platform Engineering o posiciones similares. Neo4j: Experiencia práctica diseñando, implementando y manteniendo soluciones basadas en bases de datos de grafos. Cypher: Buen dominio del lenguaje para desarrollar consultas complejas, recorrer relaciones y optimizar operaciones sobre grafos. Modelado de datos: Conocimiento de modelos Property Graph, nodos, relaciones, labels, propiedades y buenas prácticas de diseño. ETL/ELT: Experiencia desarrollando pipelines de ingesta, transformación e integración de datos. Programación: Manejo de Python o Node.js para procesamiento de datos, automatización o integración con servicios. Optimización: Conocimiento de índices, constraints, optimización de consultas y performance de bases de datos. Arquitectura de datos: Capacidad para transformar requerimientos funcionales y técnicos en modelos de datos escalables y mantenibles. Fundamentos de IA: Familiaridad con embeddings, búsqueda semántica, bases vectoriales o conceptos de RAG. Autonomía y colaboración: Capacidad analítica, resolución de problemas, documentación técnica y buena comunicación con equipos interdisciplinarios. Será un plus Experiencia con Knowledge Graphs, GraphRAG o arquitecturas de recuperación híbrida. Conocimiento de Neo4j APOC, Graph Data Science (GDS) o Neo4j Vector Index. Familiaridad con tecnologías semánticas como RDF, OWL, SKOS o SHACL. Experiencia integrando Neo4j con LangChain, LlamaIndex u otros frameworks de IA. Experiencia con Neo4j AuraDB, despliegues cloud o entornos contenerizados. Conocimiento de NLP, extracción de entidades, procesamiento documental o enriquecimiento semántico. Familiaridad con Kafka, RabbitMQ o herramientas de procesamiento distribuido. Experiencia implementando pruebas automatizadas sobre grafos, validaciones de calidad de datos o herramientas de observabilidad. Experiencia previa en proyectos de LegalTech, RegTech, compliance o plataformas de gestión de conocimiento. ¿Qué te ofrecemos en Darwoft? Contrato full-time en relación de dependencia con pago en ARS. Trabajo 100% remoto. Salario competitivo. Licencias legales y vacaciones. Días personales adicionales al año. description: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X. We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. Senior Product Designer, Knowledge Graph This is a remote position based in Germany. The Opportunity: As a Senior Product Designer at Grafana Labs, you will join a growing Product Design organization of more than 25 designers, researchers, engineers, and design leaders distributed across six continents. You will work within a 100% remote R&D organization, so strong, proactive remote communication, collaboration, facilitation, and relationship building skills will be essential to your success. As Senior Product Designer for Grafana Cloud’s Knowledge Graph, you'll design experiences for the context layer of Grafana Cloud that powers our entity graph, entity catalog and RCA workbench. Knowledge Graph automatically discovers services, infrastructure, and databases from the telemetry teams already have, maps how they depend on each other, and runs anomaly detection. This gives engineers, SREs, and their agents an up to date picture of their systems. We want anyone to be able to understand a system and resolve an incident faster, without writing queries or maintaining alert rules, not just the one person who happens to know it best. Over time, you will develop deep expertise in your product area and associated customer and user personas, use cases, and workflows, which will enable you to design tailored, role-driven experiences.
